1  JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a road traffic accident, filed petition under Sec.166 of I.M.V.Act, claiming compensation worth Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of container Lorry No.MH-05-AM-1759, alleging that on 21.08.2021 at about 1.30 p.m., when driving auto rickshaw bearing No.KA01-AK-4861 by keeping a passenger from Ibbaluru towards Silk Board on Outer ring road, near Green Bar, Agara Flyover upper ramp, HSR Layout,
driver of a Lorry bearing No.MH-05-AM-1759 negligently without barricade/stone stopped the lorry in the middle of the road, thereby made the autorickshaw to dash to the rear part of the lorry,
thereby became the reason for the accident resulting in injuries to the petitioner and inmate/passenger of the auto.
2.

sentences.text: The petitioner took first aid in a nearby hospital, then took treatment at Bowring Hospital.
As on the date of accident, petitioner being aged about 35 years, used to earn Rs.30,000/- per month by driving autorickshaw.
Regarding the accident, HSR Layout Traffic police registered a case in Cr.No.38/2021.

3. In response to the notice, the respondent No.2/insurance company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident,
nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
The respondent No.2/insurance company asserted that due to the negligent driving by the petitioner accident taken place.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1/owner of the lorry remained absent.

5. On the basis of the pleadings on21.02.2023 this Authority has framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 21.08.2021 at about 10.30 p.m., on outer ring road, near Green Bar, Agara Flyover Upper ramp, Agara, HSR layout, Bengaluru,
he met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to the actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Container Lorry bearing registration No.MH-05-AM-1759 as alleged ?
2.Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom ?
3. What order ?
6. On 18.01.2022, 12.06.2023 petitioner deposed as PW.1 and produced 13 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.13.
During cross-examination of PW.1, learned advocate appearing for insurance company get marked copy of the driving licence of the petitioner as Ex.R.1.
On 21.07.2023 and 04.08.2023 petitioner produced the evidence of Dr. Avinash Parthasarathy as PW.2 and get marked 3 documents at Exs.P.14 to P.16.
On 11.10.2023 and 03.01.2024 respondent No.2/insurance company produced the evidence of Officer as RW.1 and get produced copy of the policy at Ex.R.2.

8. On the basis of the materials placed on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... Due to the negligent use of the Autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK- 4861 by the petitioner and negligent use of Canter Lorry bearing No.MH-05-AM- 1759 at the ratio of 50 : 50, accident taken place resulting in injuries to the petitioner and inmate of autorickshaw.
Issue No.2 ...
Petitioner is entitle to receive a sum of Rs.1,09,052/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ....

sentences.text: In the evidence petitioner has stated that on 21.08.2021 at about 1.30 p.m., when driving auto rickshaw bearing No.KA01-AK-4861 by keeping a passenger from Ibbaluru towards Silk Board on Outer ring road, near Green Bar, Agara Flyover upper ramp, HSR Layout, driver of Lorry bearing No.MH-05-AM-1759 negligently without barricade/stone stopped the lorry in the middle of the road, thereby made the autorickshaw to dash to the rear part of the lorry, thereby became the reason for the accident resulting in injuries to the inmate/passenger of the auto and petitioner.

13. In the written statement, respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident and asserted that due to the sole negligent driving of the autorickshaw by the petitioner, the accident taken place.

14. In the cross-examination petitioner stated that the traffic police who was present in the spot has filed a complaint and admitted that during accident, Smt.Thanusha Shaik a passenger was present in the auto.
Petitioner submitted ignorance to the question that the passenger of the autorickshaw has filed complaint against himself and the driver of the lorry.
Petitioner admitted that in the accident, front part of the autorickshaw was completely damaged.

Petitioner denied the suggestion that the lorry was parked in the place and submitted ignorance to the question that in the accident,
back side bumper of lorry was damaged.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that he drove the autorickshaw in a rash and negligent manner with high speed, dashed the same to the rear part of the lorry.
Petitioner submitted ignorance to the question that after investigation police have filed chargesheet against himself and the driver of the lorry.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that there was neither FC nor permit to the auto as on the date of accident.
Petitioner stated that the owner of the auto sold the autorickshaw to somebody.

In the cross-examination petitioner admitted that the copy of the driving licence marked at Ex.R.1 is concerned to him and in the driving licence, nothing has been mentioned about the autorickshaw.
15.
In the evidence, PW.2 Dr.Avinash Parthasarathy stated nothing regarding reason and mode of the accident.

16. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to Cr.No.38/2021 registered by HSR Layout Traffic police on 22.08.2021 against Ashif Ali Khan-driver of the lorry bearing No.MH-05-AM-1759 and petitioner- driver of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-KA-4861,

for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.283, 279 and 338 of IPC, regarding the accident taken place on 21.08.2021 at 1.30 p.m., between rear part of the lorry bearing No.MH-05-AM-1759 and front part of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-KA-4861, resulting in injuries to Smt. Tanusha Shaik - inmate of the auto and the petitioner/driver of the autorickshaw on the basis of the statement of Smt.Tanusha Shaik.
17. Ex.P.2 is the copy of the spot mahazar recorded on 22.08.2021.
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the sketch of place of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of the Motor Vehicle Accident report dated 23.08.2021.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of the wound certificate in which reason for the injuries is noted as 'collision between passenger auto and goods vehicle'.

Ex.P.9 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by HSR layout traffic police in Cr.No.38/201 against Ashif Ali Khan s/o Mohmmed Jibrail Khan -driver of the Container Lorry No.MH- 05-AM-1759, petitioner-Yogesh s/o Manjegowda, driver of autorickshaw bearing Yogesh Alias Yogehash vs Manjit Singh Chhabra on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39247601/
4 No.KA-01-AK-4861 and Shivaram-owner of the auto

for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279, 283 and 338 of IPC, Sec.56 and 192 of M.V. Act.
18.
In this case, at this stage, there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of the police records regarding the reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 21.08.2021 at about 1.30 p.m., when petitioner was driving auto rickshaw bearing No.KA01-AK-4861 by keeping a passenger from Ibbaluru towards Silk Board on Outer ring road,
near Green Bar, Agara Flyover upper ramp, HSR Layout, due to the negligent use of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA-01-AK- 4861 by the petitioner and negligent use of the Lorry bearing No.MH-05-AM-1759 at the ratio of 50 : 50, collision taken place between the front part of the autorickshaw and rear part of the lorry, resulting in injuries to the inmate/passenger of the auto and petitioner.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 accordingly.

19. Issue No.2 : In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered left ace tabular posterior wall fracture, severe injuries to hand and legs, took first aid at St.John medical College Hospital, Bengaluru, then took treatment at Bowring Hospital, Bengaluru as an inpatient from 22.08.2021 to 08.09.2021, underwent surgery by spending more than Rs.1,25,000/-.
Petitioner stated that as on the date of accident, used to earn Rs.30,000/- by driving autorickshaw.
20. In the written statement, respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
In the cross- examination petitioner stated that his birth year is 1984 and denied the suggestion that in the accident suffered only simple injuries and never spent Rs.1,25,000/- for treatment.
Petitioner denied the suggestion about creation of medical bills for the purpose of the case.

21. In the evidence PW.2- Dr. Avinash Parthasarathy stated that on 14.06.2023 when clinically examined the petitioner, noticed that the petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 19% to the whole body and produced OPD slip, Disability assessment format and X-ray at Exs.P.14 to P.16.
In the cross-examination PW.2 admitted that he never treated the petitioner and on 14.06.2023 only to assess the disability clinically examined the petitioner.
PW.2 stated about verification of wound certificate and discharge summary of the petitioner.
22. In the evidence, RW.1 stated nothing regarding the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

23. Wound certificate, Discharge Summary, case file, prescriptions, medical bills and other medical records shows that in the accident, petitioner suffered left ace tabular posterior wall fracture, took treatment at Bowring Hospital as an inpatient from 22.082021 to 08.09.2021 by spending approximately Rs.28,104/-.

In the copy of the Aadhaar Card marked at Ex.P.13, date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 01.01.1984.
24.

As referred above, PW.2 Dr. Avinash Parthasarathy admitted that he never treated the petitioner and the petitioner has not produced any type of evidence to show either decrease in the income or loss of income subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.

Hence, I Yogesh Alias Yogehash vs Manjit Singh Chhabra on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39247601/
5 have inferred that the oral evidence of PW.2 is not sufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income (permanent functional disability).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, Rs.60,000/- is assessed towards pain and suffering, Rs.28,104/- towards treatment, Rs.15,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment charges, Rs.75,000/- (Rs.15,000 x 5 months) towards loss of income during treatment period and Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities and future happiness.
Hence, total compensation is assessed at Rs.2,18,104/- with current and future interest at 6% per annum.
25. In view of my findings recorded on Issue No.1, the petitioner is entitle to receive a sum of Rs.1,09,052/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., as compensation.
26. Copy of the policy marked at Ex.R.2 shows that as on the date of accident, lorry bearing No.MH-05-AM- 1759 had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.
In this case there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident, respondent No.1/owner of the lorry has violated any terms of the policy.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the lorry bearing No.MH-05-AM-1759 are liable pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.1,09,052/- (Rupees One Lakh Nine Thousand and Fifty Two only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6%
per annum to the petitioner towards compensation.
Respondents No.2 being the insurer of Container Lorry bearing No.MH-05-AM-1759 shall deposit compensation amount and interest within three months from today.
After deposit of compensation and interest, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 8 th day of October, 2024.)

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the lorry bearing No.MH-05-AM-1759 are liable pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.1,09,052/- (Rupees One Lakh Nine Thousand and Fifty Two only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6%
per annum to the petitioner towards compensation.
Respondents No.2 being the insurer of Container Lorry bearing No.MH-05-AM-1759 shall deposit compensation amount and interest within three months from today.
After deposit of compensation and interest, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
